records.summary: Faivel Landa died in Bialystok in 1892.

records.title: Birth of Masha Chinsky

records.title: Birth of Abraham Kantor

records.title: Rabbi Nissenbaum’s visit to Sokolka
records.summary: Rabbi Nissenbaum stayed in Sokolka for several days in 1898.

records.title: 1900 Zionist conference in Vilna

records.title: Founding of Sokolka cooperative fund

records.title: Death of Meir Markus
records.summary: Meir Markus died in Bialystok in 1901.

records.title: Mizrachi branch founded in Sokolka
records.summary: A branch was founded in Sokolka.

records.title: Appointment in Sokolka
records.summary: Chaim Meir Shmul was appointed religious teacher in Sokolka in 1902.

records.title: Yeshiva founded in Mstsislaw
records.summary: Rabbi Zvi-Hirsch Direktor founded a large yeshiva in Mstsislaw in 1903.

records.title: Death of Mordecai Neiman
records.summary: Mordecai Neiman died in Makow at age seventy in 1903.

records.title: Opening of a reformed heder
records.summary: In 1903 in Sokolka, a Hebrew teacher opened a reformed heder, but it did not continue for lack of students; the teacher's name is unclear.

records.title: Founding of the Hebrew school
records.summary: A Zionist group founded a Hebrew school in Sokolka during 1904–1905.

records.title: Rabbinic endorsement of Keren Yehoshua
records.summary: Moshe Yehuda endorsed the book Keren Yehoshua in 1905.

records.title: Elections to four Dumas
records.summary: Sokolka Jews participated in elections to four Dumas, with named representatives elected.

records.title: Permission for teacher-training courses
records.summary: Permission was obtained in 1906 to establish two-year teacher-training courses.

records.title: Opening of the courses
records.summary: The teacher-training courses opened in autumn 1907.

records.title: Death of Hillel-Moshe
records.summary: Hillel-Moshe issued instructions before his death in 1909.

records.title: 1910 collection for the Jewish National Fund
records.summary: Money was collected in Sokolka for the Jewish National Fund in 1910.

records.title: Leah Perlstein's birth
records.summary: Leah Perlstein was born in Sokolka in 1913.

records.title: First World War began
records.summary: The First World War began in 1914, ending plans to travel to the Land of Israel.

records.title: Russian army retreat from Sokolka
records.summary: The Russian army retreated from Sokolka toward Grodno during the German advance.

records.title: Burning of the flour mill and bridge
records.summary: The flour mill and bridge burned during the Russian army's retreat in 1915.

records.title: Haim Shmukler Relocates to Sokolka
records.summary: A Sokolka delegation persuaded Haim Shmukler to settle in Sokolka in 1915.

records.title: Death of Zvi Hirsch Director
records.summary: Zvi Hirsch Director died in 1915 and was buried in Kyiv.

records.title: Threatened expulsion of Grodno Jews
records.summary: In February 1915, decrees threatening the expulsion of Grodno Jews from the city loomed over them.

records.title: Birth of Yitzhak Galdshteyn
records.summary: Yitzhak Galdshteyn was born in Sokolka in 1916.

records.title: Organization of youth groups in Sokolka
records.summary: The Land of Israel Office began organizing youth groups for immigration after the war.

records.title: Death of Chaim Meir Shmul

records.title: Third Aliyah immigration
records.summary: The Third Aliyah brought immigrants to Palestine after World War I.

records.title: Communist Russian capture of Sokolka in 1919
records.summary: The communist Russian army recaptured Sokolka in 1919.

records.title: Hechalutz movement established in Sokolka
records.summary: Hechalutz arose in Sokolka during 1919–1920.

records.title: 1919 election of Yehoshua-Hashl Parbshtein
records.summary: Yehoshua-Hashl Parbshtein was elected representative and Mizrachi chairman in May 1919.

records.title: Migration to Kfar Malal

records.title: Freiheit organized in Sokolka
records.summary: Freiheit organized in Sokolka during the 1920s.

records.title: Death of Jacob Moses Margolin
records.summary: Jacob Moses Margolin died in Bialystok in 1920 at age seventy-seven.

records.title: Pioneers left the Diaspora
records.summary: Many pioneers from the town left the Diaspora for the Land of Israel in the 1920s.

records.title: Israel Goldin Emigrates to the United States
records.summary: Israel Goldin emigrated to the United States during the 1920s.

records.title: Moshe Libor migrated to Israel
records.summary: Moshe Libor immigrated to Israel during the 1920s.

records.title: Migration to Palestine
records.summary: Masha Chinsky received agricultural-pioneer training and immigrated to Palestine in 1921.

records.title: Arrival in Israel
records.summary: The author and companions arrived in Israel at the end of December 1921.

records.title: David Ardani’s departure for Israel
records.summary: David Ardani states that he left for Israel in 1923 and continued longing for Sokolka.

records.title: Move to Kfar Malal
records.summary: Masha Chinsky joined Kfar Malal in 1923 after leaving the group at Kiryat Anavim.

records.title: Move to Kfar Malal
records.summary: The group left Kinneret and joined Kfar Malal in 1924.

records.title: Joining Hashomer Hatzair
records.summary: The narrator entered Hashomer Hatzair in 1925 or 1926.

records.title: Sokolka economic crisis
records.summary: A severe economic crisis left Jewish workers, artisans, and merchants unemployed and impoverished.

records.title: Hashomer Hatzair summer camp
records.summary: Hashomer Hatzair held a summer camp in Nova Michalna in 1927.

records.title: Migration to the United States
records.summary: Moshe Yehuda Rabinowitz emigrated to the United States in the 1930s.

records.title: Appointment of Rabbi Slodzinski in Smorgon
records.summary: Rabbi Slodzinski was appointed rabbi of Smorgon in 1930.

records.title: Death of Moshe Zeev
records.summary: Moshe Zeev died in 1933 and was buried in Kfar Saba.

records.title: Chaim Yehoshua Shapiro family migration
records.summary: Chaim Yehoshua Shapiro came to Israel with his family in 1934.

records.title: Penina Kantor joins her husband in Israel
records.summary: Penina Kantor joined her husband in Israel in 1934.

records.title: Leah Perlstein receives training in Vilna
records.summary: Leah Perlstein received training in Vilna in 1935.

records.title: Departure from Sokolka for immigration
records.summary: In 1938, the narrator came to Sokolka to bid farewell to his father and family before immigrating.

records.title: German invasion of Sokolka
records.summary: German forces invaded Sokolka shortly before or during the beginning of World War II.

records.title: Outbreak of the Second World War
records.summary: The passage recalls the outbreak of the Second World War in early September 1939.

records.title: German entry into Sokolka
records.summary: German forces entered Sokolka at the beginning of September 1939.

records.title: Agricultural work at Czerniaków
records.summary: A group of seventy people left the ghetto for agricultural work at an estate.

records.title: Ghetto establishment
records.summary: Authorities ordered creation of a ghetto in 1941 across three designated streets.

records.title: German invasion of Sokolka in 1941
records.summary: German forces entered Sokolka after bombing the airfield.

records.title: Group moved to Cherniakow
records.summary: The group went to Cherniakow in summer 1941 and remained there until summer 1942.

records.title: Establishment of the Sokolka Judenrat
records.summary: In 1941, a Judenrat was chosen, with Attorney Friedberg as its head.

records.title: Evacuation from Sokolka
records.summary: Residents and Soviet units evacuated Sokolka during the German invasion.

records.title: German invasion of Sokolka
records.summary: German forces entered Sokolka after Germany declared war on Russia.

records.title: Desecration of the new study house
records.summary: German forces expelled Jews and desecrated Torah scrolls at the new study house.

records.title: Transfer to Kolbassin
records.summary: Most prisoners were transferred to Kolbassin after the ghetto existed until 1942.

records.title: Ghetto liquidation and deportation
records.summary: Residents were assembled, selected, and deported in mid-October 1942.

records.title: Deportation of Sokolka Jews to Treblinka
records.summary: Sokolka Jews were assembled and deported toward Treblinka in early December 1942.

records.title: Destruction of the deportees
records.summary: The deportees were reportedly murdered in early January 1943.

records.title: Transport of ghetto survivors to Bialystok
records.summary: About 25 people were transported by bus from the ghetto to Bialystok.

records.title: Deportation of remaining ghetto Jews to Auschwitz
records.summary: Remaining Jews were taken under guard to the railway and transported to Auschwitz.

records.title: Selection upon arrival at Auschwitz
records.summary: Most deportees were sent to gas chambers; 33 young women were initially separated.

records.title: Factory prisoners deported to Auschwitz
records.summary: On January 23, 1943, factory prisoners were loaded into wagons and deported to Auschwitz.

records.title: Gestapo assault on refugees
records.summary: Three girls and a young man were beaten by the Gestapo.

records.title: Refugees jump from a train
records.summary: Refugees from Sokolka and Krinek jumped from a train; some were wounded.

records.title: Liberation of Grodno announced
records.summary: A radio broadcast announced Grodno’s liberation before Sokolka’s liberation.

records.title: Liberation of Sokolka announced
records.summary: The radio announcer listed Sokolka among towns liberated by the Red Army.

records.title: Soviet capture of Sokolka
records.summary: Soviet forces captured Sokolka after the German retreat in 1945.

records.title: Esther Holtzman leaves Russia
records.summary: Esther Holtzman left Russia with her only son on May 1, 1946.

records.title: Return journey to Sokolka
records.summary: The narrator traveled together on July 7, 1946, and unfortunately found no Jews; Sokolka is not stated in the supplied quote.

records.title: Arrival in Israel
records.summary: Haya Leah Kaplan and her daughter arrived in Israel on July 18, 1946.

records.title: 1949 volunteer service
records.summary: Avraham Yardeni volunteered with others to assist settlements during the 1949 war.

records.title: Sokolker Aid Society annual banquet
records.summary: The society planned its annual banquet for February 2, 1957.

records.title: Death of B. Ts.
records.summary: B. Ts. died in Buenos Aires on 21 July 1961.
